name: Major cloud providers do not publish internal GPU fabric bandwidth specifications
symptom: Cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure) do not publish the internal bandwidth of their GPU cluster fabrics, making it impossible to compare cloud vs on-premises performance directly.
root_cause: Cloud providers consider their network infrastructure a competitive advantage and do not disclose internal specifications. AWS EFA documentation describes the adapter but not the underlying fabric bandwidth. GCP documentation describes the interconnect but not the per-GPU bandwidth. Azure documentation is similarly opaque.
workaround: Benchmark actual performance using NCCL tests rather than relying on published specifications. Use the cloud provider's own performance benchmarks as a reference point. For AWS, the p5.48xlarge instances with EFA provide the highest GPU fabric bandwidth, but the exact number is not published.
notes: This is an honest negative - the information is genuinely not public. Any claim about cloud fabric bandwidth should be treated as a vendor claim unless backed by independent measurement. The lack of transparency makes it difficult to make informed decisions about cloud vs on-premises deployment.
